key_concepts: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity
Total momentum of a system is the sum of the momenta of its objects
In an isolated system with no external force, total momentum is conserved
Net momentum before collision equals net momentum after collision
The law of conservation of linear momentum applies to all types of collisions
Elastic collisions conserve both momentum and kinetic energy
Inelastic collisions conserve momentum but not kinetic energy
In perfectly inelastic collisions, objects stick together and move with a common velocity
The conservation equation is m1v1 + m2v2 = m1v1' + m2v2'
Positive and negative signs indicate opposite directions of velocity
Firearm recoil demonstrates conservation of momentum
Rocket propulsion demonstrates conservation of momentum
